issues.what: The source frames were taken only at the cut edges (30.0, 30.5, 41.3, 41.8 s). None falls inside the removed span B 30.2-41.6 s. The report then says "The content of the removed footage ... [was] not established", and F3 adds "no side-by-side visual description ... is asserted from their labels". This happens even though compare_media's Next line said "say what A shows and what B shows there".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches fetching frames and then not describing them, and calling the removed content undeterminable when one get_frames call inside the span would have shown it.
issues.ideal: Request E13 frames inside the gap (e.g. 33, 36, 39 s), describe in one line what the removed footage shows and what A shows at 30.6/31.0 s, and cite those frames.

issues.what: F3 cites E26-E31 only to say they "document source samples at 30.0, 30.5, 41.3 and 41.8 s". It makes no claim about what they show, so these citations add nothing to the evidence for the deletion.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches padding the citation list with records that support no content claim.
issues.ideal: Either state what the frames show at the cut (and cite them for that), or leave them out.

issues.what: The sound difference (A 55.5-57.0 s vs B 65.7-67.2 s, similarity 0.35) is reported with "the audible nature or cause of the sound difference were not established". No ASR or sound check was run on the source E13 to characterise it. A's ASR (E12) does give sound segments (other_sound 46.1-61.95 s).
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It leaves an altered-audio point as a bare number when one more cheap tool call on the source could describe it.
issues.ideal: Run INSPECT asr on E13 and compare the sound segments around B 65.7-67.2 s with A 55.5-57.0 s before reporting.

issues.what: F4 is a recap finding ("The investigation establishes a matching source copy, an approximately localized deletion and a measured sound discrepancy") plus the ASR-empty fact. Its limitations repeat F1/F2. F1 also ends with the vague "Material A differs from it."
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches filler findings that restate earlier ones instead of adding new evidence.
issues.ideal: Drop the recap. Keep the ASR observation as one short statement only if it bears on the comparison.

issues.what: The rationales refer to "E23’s 30.2–41.6 s" and "R2’s downloaded video E23". Up to that point the rendered observations only name R2's page/video as E13. E23 shows up in no prior visible output, though it may be in evidence cards that are not rendered.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: If E23 was not visible to the student, it teaches citing ids it has not seen.
issues.ideal: Refer to the source as E13/R2 (the id the visible observations use), or cite E23 only once it is shown.

issues.what: T1 copies the full task verbatim ("The given video circulated online. Find its original source video and determine ...").
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It gives the workspace no focus, although for a single-chain A task this costs little.
issues.ideal: Restate T1 with concrete sub-steps (find a candidate from the SPACE.com caption cues, compare_media, describe each difference with times in both videos, get dates).

issues.what: READ_RECORD E30 with the boilerplate rationale "E30 is cited by the report but not attached; view it before answering." The FINISH that follows makes no use of E30, and E30 is not among the attached images there.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a ritual record read whose result never shapes the answer.
issues.ideal: Read the cited frame only to check a concrete claim (e.g. what A shows at the cut), and say in the answer what it showed.

issues.what: The verifier flagged the answer "unsupported_assertion/critical", yet the exported REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word the same as the original.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: If the flag was real, the exported answer still contains the unsupported assertion. If it was a false positive, the 'revision' label is misleading for training.
issues.ideal: Either change the flagged sentence or record that the verifier flag was rejected and why.

good_patterns: The source search query comes from visible OCR cues ("chilled to mimic", "long coast period in space", the SPACE.com watermark), not from the claim. It is precise and found the 100%-match source at R2.

compare_media was run before the candidate was treated as the source, and the removed span (B 30.2-41.6 s, 11.4 s, skipped at A 30.8 s) and the sound span (A 55.5-57.0 s vs B 65.7-67.2 s, 0.35) were copied exactly from E25, with times in both videos.

Upload and archive dates (2023-09-15) were looked up and explicitly not treated as the earliest publication ("do not establish that this was the earliest publication or the original camera recording").
The answer lists each task requirement (removed / sound changed / added-reordered-replaced none found) with honest scope limits tied to the tool's 0.5 s precision and sampling.
cannot_judge: W1-1 turn 2 rationale says "E2 confirms E1 has an audio track". E2 (presumably a metadata card) is not rendered, so I could not check it.
Whether E23 was visible to the agent in evidence cards before turn 6 (not rendered).
What the frames E26-E31 actually show (images not rendered; GIA records show media_metadata_not_pixels), so I cannot say whether the report missed visible content at the cut.
What the GIA READ_RECORD E30 returned (no observation rendered).
Which sentence the verifier's unsupported_assertion/critical referred to.
R3's partial matches and the 13 search results not shown (truncated). They do not change the choice of R2 given its 100% match.
summary: A clean, efficient A-family run: OCR-derived query, 100% source match, compare_media before calling it the source, deletion and sound-difference times copied exactly, dates fetched and not overstated as earliest. The weak spots are minor. Frames were taken only at the cut edges and never described, so the removed content is called undetermined. The sound difference was not characterised on the source. The report pads with a recap finding and citations that support no claim. GIA does a ritual READ_RECORD, and a 'revised' answer is identical to the verifier-flagged one.
